newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN says Cambodian membership "a formality".
newsitem.headline: ASEAN says Cambodian membership "a formality".

text.p: ASEAN on Monday delayed a decision on when to let Cambodia join the organisation but said the country's admission, delayed by recent political turmoil, was just a formality.

"Cambodia is part of Southeast Asia. The timing for actual membership is just a formality," Philippines foreign minister Domingo Siazon told a news conference after a meeting of foreign ministers of the nine-member grouping.

The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) postponed Cambodia's membership last month after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh after two days of bloody fighting.

Asked by reporters when Cambodia would join the grouping, Siazon said: "There's really no answer to that." He added, "Later or sooner are really relative terms. It didn't happen today. It won't happen tomorrow. It depends on further developments."

ASEAN's problem of what to do with Cambodia is complex. On Saturday, Cambodian King Norodom Sihanouk said he regarded Ung Huot, elected First Prime Minister to replace Ranariddh, as a puppet and that his son, Ranariddh, was still premier.
But the king, who reigns but does not rule, also authorised acting head of state Chea Sim to appoint Ung Huot in Ranariddh's place.
